correctness.rationale: Recurrence identities prove exact 2-adic Fibonacci valuation and rank z_k. Cassini difference identity makes projective ratios injective modulo z_k in each parity-index component. The two residue sets at k=3 lift two-to-one exactly because v2(F_zk)=k, yielding complete images and multiplicities at all depths. Taking inverses of the exact reciprocal-image balls accounts for all negative valuations, and every finite limit lies in one closed component. Exact-arithmetic checker passes bounded consistency tests but proof is the stated induction.

originality.rationale: Kumar (2024) treats the same p-adic Kepler invariant but explicitly restricts its main results to odd primes, whereas this theorem gives the omitted prime two with all nonintegral and integral branches. Lang–Lang (2013) determine scalar-cycle residue completeness and periods, not projective ratios; Garcia–Luca (2016) classify unrestricted ratios, a strictly larger object. Exact meaning-based archival database searches did not return the statement or a stronger implication; historical implicit coverage remains possible.
residual_risks: A specialized prior 2-adic projective Fibonacci orbit result may give this set without the term Kepler set.
Full body of Berend–Kumar 2025 article was not inspected; its abstract is real/complex geometric in framing (MSC 53A04).
Garcia–Luca 2016 publisher full text not accessible in this run; its all-pairs theorem is available verbatim in Kumar 2024.

value.rationale: The 2-adic Kepler set of the standard Fibonacci recurrence is the exceptional prime case of a well-motivated p-adic consecutive-ratio classification, not arbitrary computation. The result supplies a complete proper closed subset of Q2, sharp forbidden valuation levels, exact Haar measure for integer components, and all-depth uniform projective fibers; the unrestricted quotient set being dense makes the contrast structurally meaningful.
